title: Reduce behind-main collisions without a merge queue: hold or stack overlapping self tasks automatically, and report branch updates per merge
public_title: Stack overlapping self tasks and report branch updates
acceptance: Why. With strict branch protection ("require branches to be up to date", required check `ci`) and several open self pull requests, every merge makes the others fall behind main; the autopilot updates each behind pull request (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:576 calls update_branch; bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:153 sends the GitHub request) and its CI runs again. Tasks that edit the same files also start in parallel from main and collide later; firstmate has been holding them apart by judgement only (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:542). GitHub's merge queue would help, but it is not available on this personal repository. This task reduces collisions with what the workflow already has, stacked pull requests (T-143, design section 15.8), now chosen automatically from scope overlap, and adds a read-only measurement so the retro can compare before and after. Branch protection does not change.

How. For the self project only: (1) a ready task whose approved scope overlaps the scope of a task already in flight is not started in parallel from main: with self stacking allowed it is stacked on that task's open pull request, otherwise it waits; (2) self stacking is turned on by a small runtime policy file that only an answered captain card can write; (3) after a parent merges, the existing restack path moves its child onto main; (4) a read-only report estimates branch updates and CI runs per merged pull request from GitHub. Making T-260's one-front integration queue the default is deliberately not part of this task: T-260 is still in review, and that will be specified against its merged code separately. External projects are unchanged.

Terms. Self project: this repository, firstmate-workflow. In flight: a self task with a `dispatched` or `pr_opened` event and no later `merged` or `closed` event, the set bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py:134 already reads, plus candidates reserved earlier in the same dispatch run (Change 3). Stacked pull request: a pull request whose base is another open pull request's branch, not main. Restack: rebuild a child's own commits after its parent merges and retarget it (bin/lib/fm-restack.sh; design section 15.8 "T-143: operating a stack"). Approved scope of a task: the `scope` list from the task's approved spec bytes, read by the shared reader in Change 2.

Change 1, overlap rule. Add one shared function in bin/lib/fm_stack.py that decides whether two scope lists overlap. Each entry is a literal path or a glob (contains `*`, `?` or `[`). The static prefix of a glob is its leading path segments that contain no glob character (`tests/lib/*.py` → `tests/lib`; `*.md` and `**` → empty). Two entries overlap when: both are literal and equal; one is literal and the other glob matches it with fnmatch; or both are globs and one static prefix equals the other or is a whole-segment prefix of it (an empty prefix overlaps every glob). Overlapping examples: `bin/fm.sh` / `bin/fm.sh`; `tests/lib/*.py` / `tests/lib/stack.py`; `tests/**` / `tests/lib/*.py`; `*.md` / `docs/**`. Non-overlapping examples: `bin/fm.sh` / `bin/fm-merge.sh`; `tests/lib/*.py` / `tests/e2e/*.ts`; `bin/lib/x.py` / `bin/lib/xy.py`.

Change 2, approved scope reader. Add one shared reader in bin/lib/fm_stack.py, used by dispatch, `fm_stack select` and the worker check, that never reads the mutable task file on its own: if `Pins.resolve(if_present=True)` (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py) returns a pin, use that pin's spec snapshot; otherwise require `Pins.approval(None)` to return an approval and use the spec snapshot from `Pins.collect()`. Approved-branch substitution (`Pins.approved_branch_spec`, bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:381) only applies when a caller supplies a spec ref, which dispatch never does, so it is deliberately not used here; for such a task the collected snapshot is the scope, and its later pin is used once it exists. The legacy mutable-file fallback inside `Pins.preflight` (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:434-440) is never used. Any exception or missing approval makes the scope unreadable. The reader is called only when at least one self task is in flight, so a dispatch with nothing in flight reads no scope at all. bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py is not edited.

Change 3, overlap check at dispatch. bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py compares each candidate's approved scope with the approved scope of every in-flight self task, using Change 1, with no GitHub call. It does this twice: once while preparing, and again under state/dispatch.lock against the events read under the lock, adding each candidate selected earlier in the same run to the in-flight set before checking the next one, so two overlapping candidates are never selected in one batch and a competing dispatcher sees the earlier reservation. If the approved scope of the candidate or of any in-flight task cannot be read, the candidate is held with `overlap check unavailable: <task>`. External projects (FM_EXTERNAL=1) skip this check.

Change 4, what an overlap does. Dependency-only cases keep today's rule exactly: a candidate whose only conflicts are unmerged dependencies it does not overlap waits with `waits on <task>` or stacks under today's select_base rule, nested parents included as today, and a dependency is satisfied only by a `merged` event, never by `closed` (tests/dispatch.test.sh:112-116 keeps passing). New rules apply when the candidate overlaps at least one in-flight task. Let C be the overlapped in-flight tasks plus the unmerged dependencies, sorted by task number, each described as `<task> (PR #<n>)` or `<task> (no PR yet)`. Without self stacking allowed (Change 6), the candidate is held with `overlaps <list>`. With stacking allowed: if C has exactly one member and that member has an open pull request based on main, the candidate is stacked on it (Change 5); if the single member has no pull request yet, the candidate is held with `overlaps <task> (no PR yet)`; if that member's pull request is itself stacked, the candidate is held with `waits for stacked PR #<n> to reach main`; if C has two or more members, the candidate is held with `overlaps <list>`. An overlap hold is re-evaluated on every dispatch attempt and an overlapped member leaves C when it merges or closes; a dependency member leaves C only when it merges.

Change 5, stacked dispatch and the worker check. `select_base` (bin/lib/fm_stack.py:51) keeps its current signature and behaviour for its existing callers. `fm_stack select --task` (bin/lib/fm_stack.py:274-286) computes C itself with Changes 2 to 4, excluding the candidate's own dispatch record, and prints `{"name": "main"}` when C is empty, the parent `{name, head, pr}` when the candidate is stacked, and exits 65 with the hold reason otherwise; an incomplete or failed open pull request list read (only needed when a parent must be chosen) exits 65 with `open PR list unavailable`. bin/fm-worker.sh:620-640 changes in one way: for a self task without an existing pull request, the worker calls `fm_stack select` whatever the stacking policy, so a candidate reserved under one policy that starts after the policy changed is checked again and never starts overlapping work from main; with FM_EXTERNAL=1 and for workers with an existing pull request (which keep their PR's base, bin/fm-worker.sh:622-623) the path is unchanged. With stacking hold and C empty, `select` makes no GitHub call, so tests/stacking-dispatch.test.sh:24-26 keeps passing.

Change 6, self stacking policy. Today the self project has no CONVENTIONS.md, so `fm_stack_policy` returns stacking hold and force_with_lease false (bin/lib/fm-stack.sh:28-45), the `select` and `restack` actions of bin/lib/fm_stack.py read `{'stacking': 'hold'}` (bin/lib/fm_stack.py:272-273), and the autopilot keeps its self defaults (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:36; reload_policy returns early for the self project at :129-131). Add the runtime file state/autopilot/self-stack-policy.json, schema version 1, with exactly the keys `version` (integer 1, not boolean), `stacking` ("allowed" or "hold"), `force_with_lease` (boolean) and `captain_authorization` (a decision id string). One shared reader in bin/lib/fm_stack.py validates it; for the self project only, `fm_stack_policy stacking` and `fm_stack_policy force_with_lease`, both bin/lib/fm_stack.py CLI actions, and the autopilot's self policy take these two fields from it and nothing else. Every other self value (`delete_branch`, `merge_method`, `land`, `post`, `review`, required checks) stays as today, including in bin/fm-merge.sh, bin/fm-cleanup.sh and bin/lib/fm_binding.py, which are not edited. A self CONVENTIONS.md, if one ever exists, keeps today's meaning for every other field. An invalid file (symlink, unknown or missing key, wrong type, other version) is treated as stacking hold and force_with_lease false and raises one attention line per distinct problem, in English and Traditional Chinese. An absent file means today's behaviour. The file is runtime state, not pinned context: prompts and pins do not change.

Change 7, who writes the policy. Only `python3 bin/lib/fm_stack.py self-policy --decision <id> --payload <file>` writes self-stack-policy.json. The payload is the complete four-key record of Change 6 and its `captain_authorization` must equal `<id>`. The helper validates the payload schema first, then requires: the decision is an answered choice card of the self project for task T-278 with chosen A, matched to a captain `decision_made` event the same way `readiness_card_approval` does (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:93-108); and the card's details contain the SHA-256 of the exact payload bytes. It writes atomically (temporary file in the same directory, then rename). Running it again with the same decision and payload changes nothing and exits 0. Any refusal exits 65 with the reason and writes nothing. With FM_EXTERNAL=1 it refuses. After this task merges, firstmate raises that card with complete bilingual A, B and C details (A writes stacking allowed and force_with_lease true; B means firstmate revises; C writes nothing). Implementing this task turns nothing on.

Change 8, restack for the self project. With the policy allowing stacking and force_with_lease, the existing autopilot restack path (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:369-440 through bin/lib/fm-restack.sh and the `restack` action of bin/lib/fm_stack.py) runs for self stacked children after their parent merges, with its existing exit codes and wakes. Under hold or an invalid policy, a self child whose parent merged gets the existing `restack-held` attention, as external projects do today. fm-merge already keeps a parent branch while any open pull request uses it (bin/fm-merge.sh:268-272), so merging a parent never closes its child.

Change 9, read-only merge report. Add bin/lib/fm_merge_metrics.py with one command, `python3 bin/lib/fm_merge_metrics.py report --last N` (self project only; refuses with FM_EXTERNAL=1). It reads only GitHub and writes JSON lines to standard output, one per merged self pull request, newest first: `pr`, `task` (from the head branch name, or null), `merged_at`, `branch_updates` (commits on the pull request titled `Merge branch 'main' into ...`), `ci_runs` and `ci_reruns` (GitHub Actions runs for the head branch, all pages, deduplicated by run id; reruns are the sum of run_attempt minus 1), `stacked` (true when the pull request's timeline has a base change or its base at merge was not main), and `source: "github-estimate"`. A value GitHub cannot provide is null, never guessed. It writes nothing under state/ and makes no change on GitHub. The retro (T-273) can run it before and after this task to compare.

Design. Edit design/design.md section 15.8 (Pilot and advanced integration), inside its "T-143: operating a stack" subsection: describe the overlap rule and holds, the approved-scope reader, the one-level limit, the self-stack-policy file and its writer, and the read-only merge report. Add no section after the last numbered section. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md: replace the judgement-based overlap holding near :542 with a pointer to the stock overlap hold, and describe the activation card.

Tests, new behaviour. Each case names why it fails on the base; a missing helper or module is an explicit skip, never counted. (a) overlap function, every Change 1 example both ways — base has no such function. (b) approved-scope reader: a pinned scope that differs from the checkout file wins; a prospective approved snapshot is used before the first pin; no approval or a corrupt pin is unreadable — base has no reader. (c) fm-dispatch dry run, base dispatches in parallel: one overlap without policy holds with the reason; two overlaps hold listing both in task order; a member with no PR yet holds with `(no PR yet)`; dependency plus a different overlap holds; dependency and overlap on the same task stacks once under the policy; a stacked overlap parent holds with the one-level reason; the overlap hold releases on merge and on close of the member; unreadable scope holds with `overlap check unavailable`; two overlapping candidates in one run select only one; a second dispatcher preparing on old events sees the first reservation under the lock. (d) worker: under the policy, select returns the overlap parent and the child is created from it — base select ignores overlap; a candidate reserved under allowed that starts after allowed→hold, allowed→invalid or file removal exits 65 with the hold reason and starts nothing from main — base worker skips select under hold. (e) policy file: a valid file gives allowed and true to fm_stack_policy, both CLI actions and the autopilot — base always hold; invalid variants raise the bilingual attention once — base has no file. (f) self-policy helper, every refusal and success case in Change 7, plus external refusal with no write — base has no helper. (g) restack of a self child through fm-restack.sh after its parent merges under the policy — base holds it. (h) merge report: fields, pagination, run-id dedup and nulls on mocked GitHub; external refusal — base has no report. External sentinel text in a routed external project never appears in the helper or report output, attention lines or any file they write, and neither command reads the external repository.

Tests, regression (pass on the base too, assertions unchanged): absent policy file keeps hold everywhere; a self child under hold gets the existing `restack-held`; worker parent inheritance (tests/stacking-worker.test.sh:38-41); tests/stacking.test.sh, tests/stacking-dispatch.test.sh, tests/stacking-restack.test.sh, tests/stacking-binding.test.sh and direct select_base callers in tests/stacking_cases.py:119-141; merge, cleanup and binding keep today's self values with the policy file present; a pin created with the file present equals one created without it. Fixtures may be extended without changing assertions: task fixtures in tests/stacking-dispatch.test.sh, tests/dispatch.test.sh, tests/dispatch-owner.test.sh, tests/selfupdate.test.sh, tests/e2e-loop.test.sh, tests/herdr/credentials.py and tests/lib/concurrent_projects.py get the complete setup `Pins.collect()` needs wherever the reader becomes reachable, that is wherever a dispatch runs while a self task is in flight or selects more than one candidate in one run (later candidates are checked against earlier reservations): a git repository with a `main` commit holding the committed design/design.md, config.yaml and task sources that bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:190-205 snapshots, valid approval metadata (an answered captain card and its `decision_made` event, or the fixture's existing greenlit approval where the approval rules accept it), and approved scopes chosen so independent tasks do not overlap; tests/board-state.test.sh:357-361 is reviewed the same way and needs no edit because it never dispatches with a self task in flight, and pull request fixtures in tests/lib/stacking.sh gain `baseRefName: "main"`; the base ignores these additions, so the same assertions pass on it. tests/lib/external_stock.py needs no change because external dispatch skips the check. tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py (at its 1200-line limit) and tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py are not edited and keep passing; worker force-with-lease callers (bin/fm-worker.sh:1147, :2311), tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, tests/worker-external-catchup.test.sh and tests/external-private-text.test.sh keep passing.

Records and tasks already in flight. Migration rewrites nothing: no existing pin, card, dispatch receipt, pull request base or commit history changes when the policy file is written, changed or removed; a test compares them byte for byte before and after activation and before and after removal. Operational restacks are allowed for every one-level self child whose parent merges while the policy allows stacking, including children created before activation (there is no creation marker; eligibility is the parent having merged), and the child is retargeted to its parent's base, which is main for a one-level child (bin/lib/fm_stack.py:153-156). An existing child stacked two levels deep is restacked onto its parent's base, which is the middle pull request's branch, exactly as today; this task creates no such stacks. Workers with an existing pull request keep its base (bin/fm-worker.sh:622-623); workers that start a new pull request run the Change 5 check under the policy in effect when they start. Transition tests in tests/self-stack-policy.test.sh: allowed to hold (no new stacks; an existing one-level child gets `restack-held`), allowed to invalid (same, plus one attention), file removed (today's behaviour, records unchanged byte for byte), a pre-activation one-level child restacked onto main after activation, a pre-activation two-level child restacked onto the middle branch, and a pre-activation worker with an existing pull request keeping its base.
Privacy. All new behaviour is self-only. No external project text, name or path enters committed files, the report or attention lines.

Fixture setup in tests/crew-end-to-end.test.sh. Why: Change 5 makes every self worker without a pull request run `fm_stack select`, which stops a task whose approved scope overlaps a task still in flight. That test runs two real worker rounds in one repository; both fixture tasks declare scope `src/**` (lines 54-55), T-1 stays in flight after its round (line 130), and the test expects T-2's round to exit 0 (line 132), so it would now exit 65. How: change only that test's setup so the two fixture tasks no longer overlap: give T-2 a scope that does not overlap T-1's (for example `lib/**`), and seed whatever approval record the approved scope reader (Change 2) needs for both tasks, using the same helpers the test already uses. Do not change any assertion, expected value, worker invocation or the mock adapter's behaviour; the test must still prove two real worker rounds start in one root. This is interface maintenance for Change 5, not new-behaviour evidence: it is green on the base and must stay green on the head.

Canary fixture scopes in bin/fm-canary.sh. Why: the canary runs one real self worker round per hostile mode (tree, git, truncate, fill-tmp, empty-var) in one repository, and every fixture task it writes declares the same scope `src/**` (bin/fm-canary.sh:472). Under Change 5 the first round's task stays in flight, so every later self round now overlaps it and fm-worker.sh exits 65 before the hostile mode runs; tests/canary.test.sh then reports four self modes as not restored (CI run 37961869733, shard 3). The same would happen to a real canary run. How: change only the fixture spec that bin/fm-canary.sh writes for each mode so that the scopes do not overlap, by giving each mode its own directory: `src/<mode>/**` (for example `src/git/**`). Change nothing else in bin/fm-canary.sh beyond the closed event below: not the modes, the order, the external fixture, the adapter, the SPEC-OK binding or the restoration checks. tests/canary.test.sh keeps every assertion unchanged and must pass on the head. This is interface maintenance for Change 5, not new-behaviour evidence. The canary self fixture has no gate contract, so no fixture task has a readable approved scope. After each self mode is recorded, bin/fm-canary.sh appends a captain `closed` event for that mode's task to the fixture's own events log, in the same way it already appends `greenlit`, so the next self mode starts with nothing in flight. This is the only other change to bin/fm-canary.sh.

Selector compatibility with local fixtures and existing task IDs. Why: Change 5 runs `fm_stack select` for every self worker without a pull request, so it now meets callers it never met before. The canary's origin is a local bare repository with no GitHub mapping (bin/fm-canary.sh:465, :477), and its tasks and the worker fixtures use non-numeric IDs such as T-DESTROYTREE (bin/fm-canary.sh:485) and T-Z (tests/lib/worker.sh:58), which pin validation already accepts (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:113). How: (1) bin/lib/fm-stack.sh and bin/lib/fm_stack.py resolve the GitHub repository only when choosing a parent actually needs a GitHub read. Without resolving it, select succeeds when the candidate has no unmerged dependency and overlaps nothing in flight (the member set C is empty), and holds when the hold reason is decided locally (policy or the number of conflicts). Dependency-only stacking keeps its repository-qualified open-PR lookup exactly as today (tests/stacking-dispatch.test.sh:28-30 stays green unchanged). (2) fm_stack.py accepts every task ID that pin validation accepts; conflict ordering stays deterministic: numeric IDs by number first, then any other ID in plain string order. No overlap check is skipped for any ID. Tests: in tests/lib/stack_overlap.py, a no-conflict candidate in a repository whose origin is a local path reaches its worker (exit 0) without a repository lookup; two overlapping non-numeric IDs still hold; the ordering rule above is asserted; and an allowed dependency-only candidate still performs the repository-qualified PR lookup. These are new-behaviour cases and must fail on the base for a behavioural reason. tests/worker-lifecycle.test.sh and tests/canary.test.sh stay unchanged and must pass on the head.
